artifacts.summary: The BL-plus time-reflection transport: fifteen declarations across five phases, three plan deviations, the full verification record, and five follow-ups.

completion_data.completion_summary: Built the paper's one-sentence extension of lem:time-reflection to the Stability language as fifteen Lean declarations with the plan's pinned signatures: the carrying lemma promoted to Semantics/Reversal.lean with its paper-faithful image form, a new PlusLanguage/PlusReversal.lean carrying the seven-case plusTruthAt_rev and the L-plus thm:TR-valid family, TaskFrame.deterministic_rev with the Determined- and deterministic-class closures, and the TR-route decision recorded after verifying the alternative route elaborates. Un-narrowed full build green at 2859 jobs with zero sorry and the axiom count unchanged; build-backed check-module-invariants.sh prints ALL CHECKS PASSED.

memory_candidates.content: lake-build-guard.sh can REPLAY a green result that never covered an edited file, and guard exit 0 plus a 'Build completed successfully' line is not sufficient evidence that a build covered your sources. The guard's post_fingerprint is taken at build END, so a source edit landing mid-build (after its own module has already compiled) is captured by that fingerprint and makes the tree look 'unchanged' to the next waiter. A subsequent identical invocation then satisfies all three replay conditions and emits 'REPLAY: sharing result from holder pid N, age Ns, recorded exit status 0' without running lake at all -- and the replayed log is byte-identical to the original, per-target timings included, so nothing in the log reveals it. The only tells are the REPLAY: line on stderr and the .olean mtime still predating the source. Two rules follow: (1) never edit a source file while a guarded build is in flight; (2) verify every build with a three-tier check -- guard exit code, success line plus zero 'error:' count, AND an .olean-newer-than-source test for every module the task touched. Use --no-share to force a real build when a replay is suspected.

Before planning how to REGISTER a new Lean module, read the README of the component directory you are adding it to -- it commonly documents registration surfaces the plan would otherwise discover as gate failures. Adding FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/PlusReversal.lean tripped check-metalogic-cycles.sh with 'unlayered module: the per-file table LANGUAGE_FILE_LAYERS has no row', fixed by adding the row to scripts/measure-refactor-partitions.py AND the matching name to ORGANISATION.md together, as the checker's own remediation text instructs. That requirement was NOT undocumented: FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/README.md states in bold that 'A new file in this directory needs a row in that table'. Note also that the checker SHORT-CIRCUITS -- while a module is unlayered it reports only the unlayered-module failure and suppresses the upward-import-set measurement entirely, so a second, pre-existing failure can stay hidden until the layer row lands.

A gate that exits 0 can be a VACUOUS pass, and a plan clause saying 'script X exits 0, run un-narrowed' does not by itself buy evidence. .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh exits 0 while printing 'PASS -- 0 check(s), 0 failure(s)' because every gate it runs is driven by a registry loaded from .claude/scripts/gate-registry.data, and that file is absent from BOTH the deployed tree and the source store; the script documents the degradation ('A missing lib degrades to an empty gate_registry_ids'), so the empty run is by design rather than a crash. An exit 0 over zero checks satisfies such a clause's LETTER while supplying strictly less evidence than the narrowed subset pass the clause was written to forbid. When a verification clause names an aggregator, check the check COUNT, not just the exit code, and obtain coverage by running the member gates individually if the aggregator is empty.

A generated inventory block marked `rows=loose` is NOT inert: it lists the files sitting directly in that directory, so an edit to any AGGREGATOR file at the directory's root moves its line counts, not only adding or removing files. A plan that predicted three moved blocks (two component READMEs plus the root) was wrong twice: FormalSystem/README.md moved because Phase 1 edited FormalSystem/Semantics.lean and FormalSystem/OpenLanguage.lean -- two files sitting directly in FormalSystem/ -- and FormalSystem/Metalogic/README.md moved once a file under Metalogic/Deterministic/ grew. Derive the moved set by running `check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory` and reading `git status --short`, rather than reasoning about block options in advance. Relatedly, a pre-commit gate keyed on whole-tree line counts (here typst/generated/status.typ) fires at the FIRST phase commit that moves a .lean line count, so a plan that schedules its regeneration only in a final generated-surfaces phase has an unreachable step.
